datasets.name: Miami Dade County Employee Pay Information (open data feature service)
datasets.what: One row per County employee under the Mayor: name, title, company, department, annual salary, gross pay last paycheck, gross year to date. 23,674 rows at the last edit. Constitutional offices (Sheriff, Supervisor of Elections, Property Appraiser, Tax Collector, Clerk) left the County payroll on January 7, 2025 and the dataset says to contact each office for current pay.
datasets.asOf: 2026-10-14 (layer lastEditDate 1792060476550); pay fields are the most recent pay period and calendar year to date

datasets.name: Employee Salary Search
datasets.what: Search front end on the same data: by department, employee name and title; shows gross pay last paycheck, adjusted gross (health and FRS), YTD gross and adjusted YTD gross for the most recent pay period. The page says it 'should not be used as a substitute for public records requests.'
datasets.asOf: most recent pay period; 26 pay periods a year

datasets.name: Online Checkbook
datasets.what: Every County payment and disbursement for goods or services plus revenue and refund distributions, by payee. Power BI viewer; search by payee name, payment date range, amount range, disbursement number range. 'Data is available from October 1, 2006 to end of prior month' (Aviation and Water and Sewer from October 1, 2007). 'Data is uploaded monthly.' Unaudited and unconsolidated. No download or API; Police and OIG exempt records are excluded.
datasets.asOf: October 1, 2006 through end of prior month, updated monthly

datasets.name: Appendix V: Active Goods and Services Contracts (FY 2026-27 Proposed Budget)
datasets.what: Every active goods and services contract: contract ID, description, user departments, begin and expire dates, contract amount. Contract IDs only, no vendor names.
datasets.asOf: contracts active at the July 2026 proposed budget

datasets.name: Clerk of the Court and Comptroller employee salaries
datasets.what: Power BI dashboard of all current Clerk employees (an independent constitutional office since January 7, 2025): name, job title, department, annual base salary, last biweekly gross pay, YTD gross pay. Updated biweekly after payroll. No download.

levers.how: Speak at the two September budget hearings in the Commission Chambers, Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1st Street, second floor; register on the first floor and you are escorted up. The second hearing adopts the millage, the general fund, UMSA and proprietary budget ordinances and, under Item H, the FY 2026-27 pay plan and fee schedules.
levers.rules: Hearings at 5:01 p.m.; 2026 dates were Sept 3 and Sept 17 (R-627-26); proposed 2027 dates are Sept 9 and Sept 23. 'Interested parties may appear and be heard' under the Board's Rules of Procedure. Accommodation requests to 305-375-2035 or agendco@miamidade.gov in advance.
levers.deadline: At the hearing; the Mayor's proposed budget is due to the Commission by July 15 and the six August community budget meetings are 6 to 8 p.m.

levers.how: Read Appendix A of the budget (positions by department, prior year and proposed) and Appendix B (salary and fringe by department), then each department narrative in Volumes 2 and 3 which 'describes all position changes in detail.'
levers.rules: Appendix A is in thousands of dollars; FY 2026-27 proposed 31,942 positions against 31,998 in FY 2025-26, a countywide net decrease of 56 (418 added, 474 reduced). The adopted FY 2026-27 volumes were not yet posted on 2026-10-23.
levers.deadline: Proposed budget posted in July; adopted volumes follow the September hearings

levers.how: Payroll by employee and the full check register are public records under Chapter 119. Submit and track a request on the County portal; the salary search page says it 'should not be used as a substitute for public records requests.'
levers.rules: 'Pursuant to Florida Statute 119, charges may be assessed for labor and copies'; if charges apply you are contacted with an estimate first. Clerk, Sheriff, Property Appraiser, Tax Collector and Supervisor of Elections payroll is requested from each constitutional office.

levers.how: Contract awards over the Mayor's delegated authority come to the Commission as agenda items (first to a committee, then the full Board). Speak during the 'reasonable opportunity to be heard' period under Rule 6.06 at the start of the meeting, or for public hearing items register at the Agenda Coordination table at least 15 minutes before the item.
levers.rules: Rule 6.06: 2 minutes per speaker, 10 minutes per side; registration closes 30 minutes after the noticed start. Public hearing items: up to 5 minutes (Rule 6.04). Active contracts are listed with ID, term and amount in Appendix V.
levers.deadline: Register the morning of the meeting; agenda posted about 7 days ahead

levers.how: Each collective bargaining agreement is approved by Commission resolution after the unit ratifies it; the seven 2026-2029 agreements came as resolutions R-561-26 through R-567-26 in June and July 2026. Speak under Rule 6.06 when the item is on the agenda. Negotiation sessions are noticed on the Clerk's site.
levers.rules: Current County agreements run June 1, 2026 through May 31, 2029. The labor relations page posts each agreement PDF and the job classifications it covers.
levers.deadline: Before the Board vote on the ratification item

levers.how: Report fraud or waste to the Office of the Inspector General (24-hour line 305-579-2593, online fraud form, 601 NW 1st Court 22nd floor). The Office of the Commission Auditor (created by the 2002 charter amendment, 24 positions, 305-375-4354) audits departments and contracts for the Board and posts reports. Internal Compliance posts department audit reports.
levers.rules: The OIG page notes that under Florida law e-mail addresses are public records. Audit reports are posted by each office, not in one register (see the County audit index).

notes: Dataset access: the Employee Pay feature service answers ArcGIS REST queries (count, orderBy, outFields); grouped statistics by department could not be read here because the fetch tool returned a cached response for the same path, so department payroll comes from the budget book (Appendix B salary, in thousands, converted to dollars) and department positions from Appendix A. Appendix B salary was captured only for the 15 largest departments; payroll is null for the rest. Highest paid titles are the top five AnnualSalary rows from the feature service as of 2026-10-14. 'Payroll total' is the FY 2026-27 proposed Salary category (3,339,858 thousand) from Appendix B; fringe is a further 1,702,517 thousand. The Online Checkbook is a Power BI viewer with no export, so no 'total paid to vendors' by year could be read; vendors.top is Appendix V active contracts by contract ID and full-term amount (the PDF prints no vendor names and the fetch truncated after about 40 rows at R-681-21), period and total are therefore not one year's payments. The adopted FY 2026-27 budget volumes and pay plan were not posted on the budget site on 2026-10-23; all staffing numbers are from the July 2026 proposed budget. Union items 261088, 261089 and 261091 returned client errors; IAFF 1403 and PBA (Sheriff) 2026 successor agreements were not found. Board vote tallies on the CBA resolutions were not legible in the minutes PDFs. Clerk payroll is a separate Power BI dashboard (constitutional office). Sources saved under scratchpad payments-src (county-*.txt).
